sections.normalized_html:
Every interval can be expressed as an inequality. We use the following notations:

  • Parentheses [MATH: {\color{red}{(}}\phantom{0} \phantom{0}{\color{red}{)}}] to indicate that the endpoints are not included.

  • Brackets [MATH: {\color{blue}{[}}\phantom{0} \phantom{0}{\color{blue}{]}}] to indicate that the endpoints are included.

Our interval contains only parentheses. So, the endpoints are not included.

[MATH: x\in {\color{red}{(}}1, 5{\color{red}{)}}]

Therefore, our interval can be expressed as the following inequality:

[MATH: 1 \,\,{\color{red}{< }}\,\, x \,\,{\color{red}{< }}\,\, 5]

sections.normalized_html:
Every inequality can be expressed as an interval. We use the following notations:

  • Parentheses [MATH: {\color{red}{(}}\phantom{0} \phantom{0}{\color{red}{)}}] if the endpoints are not included.

  • Brackets [MATH: {\color{blue}{[}}\phantom{0} \phantom{0}{\color{blue}{]}}] if the endpoints are included.

Our inequality contains only "or equal to" symbols. So, the endpoints [MATH: 1] and [MATH: 4] are included.

[MATH: 1\,\, {\color{blue}{\le}} \,\, x \,\, {\color{blue}{\le}} \,\, 4]

Therefore, we can express our inequality in interval notation as follows:

[MATH: {\color{blue}{[}}1,4{\color{blue}{]}}]

More formally, we can also write

[MATH: x\in [1,4].]

items.readable_text:
Content:
Some intervals may include one parenthesis and one bracket.

Content:
For example, consider the following interval:

Content:
[MATH: {\color{blue}{{\big[}}} 1,4 {\color{red}{\big)}}]

Content:
To express this interval as an inequality, we note the following:

Content:
- The left bracket [MATH: \,\color{blue}[\,] tells us that left endpoint [MATH: 1] is included in the interval. Therefore, we use [MATH: {\color{blue}{\leq}}] for this endpoint.
- The right parenthesis [MATH: \,\color{red})\,] tells us that the right endpoint [MATH: 4] is not included in the interval. Therefore, we use [MATH: {\color{red}{< }}\,] for this endpoint.

Content:
Therefore, the inequality that corresponds to the given interval is

Content:
[MATH: 1 \,\,{\color{blue}{\leq }}\,\, x \,\,{\color{red}{\lt}}\,\, 4.]

Content:
The interval can be graphed as follows:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/6ae2015b1e03f53fbed7ef67c9c93fc9]

Content:
Intervals with one bracket and one parenthesis are called half-open (or half-closed).

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Every interval can be expressed as an inequality. We use the following notations:

  • Parentheses [MATH: {\color{red}{(}}\phantom{0} \phantom{0}{\color{red}{)}}] to indicate that the endpoints are not included.

  • Brackets [MATH: {\color{blue}{[}}\phantom{0}\phantom{0}{\color{blue}{]}}] to indicate that the endpoints are included.

For the given interval

[MATH: {\color{red}{{\big(}}} -4, \sqrt2\, {\color{blue}{\big]}}]

we note the following:

  • The left endpoint [MATH: -4] is not included in the interval. Therefore, we use [MATH: {\color{red}{\lt}}\,.]

  • The right endpoint [MATH: \sqrt2] is included in the interval. Therefore, we use [MATH: {\color{blue}{\leq }}\,.]

Therefore, the inequality that corresponds to the given interval is [MATH: -4 \,\,{\color{red}{\lt }}\,\, y \,\,{\color{blue}{\leq}}\,\, \sqrt 2.]

Content:
Some intervals may include one parenthesis and one bracket.

Content:

Content:

Content:
To express this interval as an inequality, we note the following:

Content:

- The right parenthesis [MATH: \,\color{red})\,] tells us that the right endpoint [MATH: 4] is not included in the interval. Therefore, we use [MATH: {\color{red}{< }}\,] for this endpoint.

Content:
Therefore, the inequality that corresponds to the given interval is

Content:
[MATH: 1 \,\,{\color{blue}{\leq }}\,\, x \,\,{\color{red}{\lt}}\,\, 4.]
